Description: AR invoice is for a customer location
Business Logic: Links AR invoice to the customer retail location. Functional (each invoice is for one customer). Used for customer-level revenue analysis and collections tracking.

Description: AR invoice generated for a shipment
Business Logic: Links AR invoice to the shipment that triggered it. Connects fulfillment execution to revenue recognition. Each shipment generates an AR invoice upon delivery.

Description: AR invoice has line items
Business Logic: One-to-many: AR invoice header to its line items. THIS is where SKU-level revenue data lives — unit_price and line_amount ARE populated (unlike order_lines). The source of truth for product-level revenue attribution.

Description: AR invoice line is for a specific SKU
Business Logic: Links AR invoice line to the SKU sold. This is the revenue attribution join — line_amount here is the actual revenue for this SKU sale. Critical for product profitability analysis.

Description: Receipt of payment against an AR invoice
Business Logic: Links receipt to the AR invoice being collected. Completes the order-to-cash financial cycle. Compare receipt amount against invoice total_amount for collection rate analysis.

Description: Trade deduction references a SKU (denormalized for analytics)
Business Logic: Denormalized SKU reference on deductions for analytics. Enables trade spend by SKU without joining through invoice lines. Cross-domain: deductions (demand) reference SKUs (supply).

Description: Trade deduction is calculated from a trade program
Business Logic: Links each deduction to the trade program that generated it. deduction_amount = list_price_per_case × quantity_cases × trade_program.rate_pct.

Description: Trade deduction linked to a specific promo event (nullable)
Business Logic: Links promo_fund deductions to the specific promo event (when the invoice falls within the event window). NULL for non-promo deductions and promo_fund deductions outside event windows.

Description: Trade deduction applied to an AR invoice
Business Logic: Links deductions to the AR invoice they apply to. Combined with ar_line_number, identifies the specific invoice line. Key invariant: SUM(deduction_amount) per invoice = gross_revenue - net_revenue.

Description: Demand forecast for a specific SKU
Business Logic: Links demand forecast to the SKU being forecasted. Used for demand planning and forecast accuracy analysis.

Description: Disposition action for a specific return
Business Logic: Links disposition log to its return. Records the final outcome of returned goods after inspection (restock, destroy, rework, donate).

Description: Inventory at a location (polymorphic: plant, DC, or retail)
Business Logic: Polymorphic location with explicit type discriminator. location_type values: plant → plants table, rdc → distribution_centers (type='rdc'), customer_dc → distribution_centers (type='customer_dc'), store → retail_locations. Store inventory is ~98% of records.

Description: Inventory snapshot for a specific SKU
Business Logic: Links inventory snapshots to the SKU being tracked. Each inventory row is a point-in-time snapshot for a specific SKU at a specific location.

Description: Order delivered to a retail location
Business Logic: Links order to its delivery retail location. Non-polymorphic — this is the clean FK for store-level analysis. Functional (each order is delivered to one location).

Description: Order placed through a sales channel
Business Logic: Links order to its source channel. CAUTION: source_id is polymorphic — values 1-7 point to channels table, values 67+ point to retail_locations table. No discriminator column. This relationship is only valid when source_id <= 7.

Description: Order has line items
Business Logic: One-to-many: order header to its line items. Lines specify SKUs and quantities. WARNING: unit_price on order_lines is ALWAYS ZERO — do not use for revenue calculations.

Description: Order line is for a specific SKU
Business Logic: Links order line to the SKU being ordered. Used for product-level demand analysis (volume only — not revenue).

Description: Promo event promotes a specific SKU
Business Logic: Links promo events to the SKU being promoted. Cross-domain: promo events (demand/trade_management) reference SKUs (supply/product). lift_pct on the event estimates incremental volume for this SKU.

Description: Promo event is funded by a trade program
Business Logic: Links promo events to their parent trade program. All promo events must reference a promo_fund-type program. The parent program's rate_pct is the base deduction; the event's incremental_spend is the additional cost.

Description: Return originated from a retail location
Business Logic: Links return to the retail location where it originated. Functional (each return comes from one store). Used for return rate analysis by store.

Description: Return has line items
Business Logic: One-to-many: return header to its line items. Each line records the returned SKU, quantity, and condition assessment.

Description: Return line is for a specific SKU
Business Logic: Links return line to the SKU being returned. Used for product-level return analysis and quality tracking.

Description: Return is sent to a distribution center
Business Logic: Links return to the distribution center where it is processed (inspected, dispositioned). Functional (each return is sent to one DC). Returns flow from retail locations to DCs for processing.

Description: Shipment originates from a location (polymorphic: plant, DC, or retail)
Business Logic: Polymorphic origin without an explicit type column. Use route_type to infer origin type: plant_to_* implies Plant origin, rdc_to_* implies DistributionCenter (RDC) origin, customer_dc_to_* implies DistributionCenter (customer DC) origin.

Description: Shipment has line items
Business Logic: One-to-many: shipment header to its line items. Each line records an SKU, quantity in cases, and weight. Used for fulfillment verification and logistics weight planning.

Description: Shipment line carries a specific SKU
Business Logic: Links shipment line to the SKU being shipped. Used for product-level logistics analysis and fulfillment tracking.

Description: Shipment delivered to a location (polymorphic: plant, DC, or retail)
Business Logic: Polymorphic destination without an explicit type column. Use route_type to infer destination type: *_to_rdc implies DistributionCenter (RDC), *_to_customer_dc implies DistributionCenter (customer DC), *_to_store implies RetailLocation.

Description: Trade program belongs to a sales channel
Business Logic: Links trade programs to their sales channel. Each channel has multiple programs (scan, rebate, promo, slotting, off-invoice) that together decompose the total trade discount rate.

Description: GL journal entry posts to a chart of accounts entry
Business Logic: Links GL journal entries to their chart of accounts classification. IMPORTANT: join key is account_code (VARCHAR), NOT id (INTEGER). ~48M journal entries across 14 accounts.

Description: Variance recorded against an AP invoice
Business Logic: Links variance records to the AP invoice with discrepancies. ~8% of invoices have price variances, ~5% have quantity variances.

Description: AP invoice matches a goods receipt
Business Logic: Links AP invoice to the goods receipt it matches. Part of three-way match: PO ↔ GR ↔ AP Invoice. When all three agree on quantity and cost, the invoice is approved for payment.

Description: AP invoice is from a supplier
Business Logic: Links AP invoice to the supplier who issued it. Functional (each invoice is from one supplier). Used for supplier spend analysis and payables tracking.

Description: AP invoice has line items
Business Logic: One-to-many: AP invoice header to its line items. Lines detail what was invoiced — ingredient, quantity, unit cost, line amount. Used for three-way match at the line level.

Description: AP invoice line is for a specific ingredient
Business Logic: Links AP invoice line to the ingredient being invoiced. Used for ingredient-level cost tracking and variance analysis against PO terms.

Description: Payment made against an AP invoice
Business Logic: Links payment to the AP invoice being settled. Completes the procure-to-pay financial cycle. ~10% of payments include early-pay discount (discount_amount > 0).

Description: Goods receipt delivered to a plant
Business Logic: Links goods receipt to the plant that received the materials. Functional (each GR is at one plant). Confirms physical receipt at the manufacturing site.

Description: Goods receipt received from a shipment
Business Logic: Links goods receipt to the inbound shipment that delivered it. Functional (each GR comes from one shipment). Connects logistics to receiving.

Description: Goods receipt has line items
Business Logic: One-to-many: GR header to its line items. Each line records actual quantity received per ingredient. Used for receipt verification against PO lines.

Description: GR line received a specific ingredient
Business Logic: Links each GR line to the ingredient received. Used for material traceability — confirms which ingredient was physically received.

Description: Purchase order delivered to a plant
Business Logic: Links each purchase order to the receiving plant. Functional (each PO is delivered to exactly one plant). Determines where procured materials enter the manufacturing network.

Description: Purchase order placed with a supplier
Business Logic: Links each purchase order to its supplier. Functional (each PO has exactly one supplier). This is the procurement relationship in the procure-to-pay chain.

Description: Purchase order has line items
Business Logic: One-to-many: PO header to its line items. Each line specifies an ingredient, quantity, and unit cost. Lines are the detail level for three-way match verification.

Description: PO line is for a specific ingredient
Business Logic: Links each PO line to the ingredient being ordered. Used for ingredient-level procurement analysis and traceability from supplier through to production.

Description: Supplier offers an ingredient at a given cost/lead time
Business Logic: Many-to-many sourcing matrix between suppliers and ingredients. Each edge carries commercial terms (unit_cost, lead_time_days, min_order_qty). Multiple suppliers may offer the same ingredient — this is the basis for procurement optimization.

Description: Batch produced at a plant
Business Logic: Links batch to the plant where it was produced. For plant-level production volume and capacity utilization analysis.

Description: Batch consumed ingredients during production
Business Logic: Actual ingredient consumption during production. quantity_kg = total kg consumed. Expected = formula_ingredients.quantity_kg × batches.quantity_kg (per-case × cases). Mass balance: sum of inputs should approximate batch output / yield_percent. Use for planned-vs-actual analysis and full traceability.

Description: Batch produced from a work order
Business Logic: Links batch to its originating work order. A work order may produce multiple batches. This connects production execution to production planning.

Description: Batch produces a product (polymorphic: SKU or BulkIntermediate)
Business Logic: Polymorphic: batch produces either a SKU (product_type='finished_good') or a BulkIntermediate (product_type='bulk_intermediate' or 'premix'). The product_type column is the type discriminator.

Description: Batch uses a specific formula
Business Logic: Links batch to the formula used for production. Through the formula, connects to ingredient requirements and the product being made.

Description: Formula produces a product (polymorphic: SKU or BulkIntermediate)
Business Logic: Polymorphic: formula produces either a SKU (bom_level=0) or a BulkIntermediate (bom_level=1 or 2). The bom_level column is the type discriminator. 500 formulas produce SKUs, 49 produce primary bulk intermediates, 13 produce premix sub-intermediates.

Description: Formula requires ingredients (BOM)
Business Logic: BOM explosion semantics — quantity_kg is per-batch requirement. For total requirements, multiply through the hierarchy via N-level traversal (formula → sub-formula → ingredients). IMPORTANT: ingredient_id is polymorphic — points to ingredients table (raw materials), bulk_intermediates table (bom_level=1 primary bulks or bom_level=2 premixes). No discriminator column; must LEFT JOIN both tables. Diamond dependencies exist — a raw material may appear in both a premix formula AND directly in its parent bulk formula.

Description: Production line is located at a plant
Business Logic: Links production lines to their plant. Functional (each line is at one plant). The sql_filter (is_active=true) ensures only operational lines are considered. line_type on the production line determines category capability.

Description: Route segment ends at a location (polymorphic)
Business Logic: Polymorphic destination of transport network edges. Destination types: plant, rdc, customer_dc, store. Retail locations (store) are destination-only nodes — the final delivery point. Note: destination_type value is 'store' not 'retail'.

Description: Route segment originates from a location (polymorphic)
Business Logic: Polymorphic origin of transport network edges. Origin types: supplier (100 segments), plant (42 segments), rdc (38 segments), customer_dc (3,817 segments). Suppliers are origin-only nodes — they ship TO the network but nothing ships TO them.

Description: SKU supersedes another SKU (alias/replacement chain)
Business Logic: Self-referential alias chain for SKU replacements. 21 SKUs (~4.2%) with -OLD suffix have supersedes_sku_id pointing to their replacement. Chains are depth-1 (one rename generation — no multi-generation recursive chains). Chain is acyclic and asymmetric. Used to resolve current SKU code from legacy codes.

Description: Work order is executed at a plant
Business Logic: Links work order to the plant where production occurs. Functional (each WO is at one plant). Determines manufacturing site for capacity planning.

Description: Work order uses a specific formula
Business Logic: Links work order to the formula (recipe/BOM) being produced. Functional (each WO uses one formula). Through the formula, determines what product is being made and what ingredients are needed.
